# round8.md — VisualCore Premium Procedural Games, Round 8
**Canonical root deliverable:** `round8.md` · **Proposed as of 2026-11-10** · **25 new premium games** · **complete only after `round7.md` implementation AND full D1/D2/D3 device campaign.**
**TRUTH STATUS:** This is a detailed engineering specification, not a report of implemented software. Original scores are subjective prior concept estimates; new supplemental scores are conservatively discounted analog estimates. No hardware performance, release, or app store success is claimed. All future pass claims must be supported by inspectable command/test outputs.
**Nonnegotiable invariants:** all hero artwork generated through code with VisualCore and GLES/ANGLE→Metal; no manual 3D assets, texture artists, image models, ads, tracking/ad SDKs, in-app purchases, subscriptions or mandatory network access; original paid-once offline play; do not use Claude CLI; Claude Desktop Code tab runs actual `/speckit-*` skills sequentially.

## Reading order and complete source-of-truth hierarchy
1. Read actual root CLAUDE.md and README.md and every preceding round file; verify installed .claude/skills and active feature location.
2. Independently verify the previous `round7.md` implementation lock and its 25×3 actual device outcomes. Absence or blocker means stop THIS round and resume earlier work.
3. Shared additions are proposed extensions, not directives to create duplicate packages. First inspect existing files and reuse established code; document any truly missing functions and consumers.
4. Use the exact 12 shared Spec Kit feature sequences before 25 game implementations, and the exact 10×8 game-feature prompts printed below.
5. Implement all targets and verify on host and simulators; only after a cryptographically hashed implementation-lock manifest run D1 whole round, then D2 whole round, then D3 whole round.
6. Keep the 25 complete argument outlines and 500-game baseline research notes in this file; evidence categories matter—no generic comparable is a sales forecast.

### 2.1 Shared public contracts and deterministic test hooks
```swift
public struct R8Seed: Codable, Hashable { public let value: UInt64 }
public struct R8Tick: Codable, Comparable { public var value: UInt64 }
public struct R8PuzzleAction: Codable {
    public let tick: UInt64; public let controlID: String
    public let normalizedCoordinates: SIMD2<Double>; public let value: Double
}
public struct R8RenderSnapshot: Codable {
    public let tick: UInt64; public let worldSeed: UInt64
    public let semanticObjectIDs: [UInt64]; public let qualityTier: Int
}
public protocol R8DeterministicGame {
    associatedtype State: Codable; associatedtype Action: Codable
    mutating func apply(_ action: Action) throws
    mutating func advanceFixedTick() throws
    func winPredicate() -> Bool
    func canonicalReplayDigest() -> String
}
// Adapt to audited actual existing VisualCore interfaces. NEVER duplicate
// render context or treat these illustrative interfaces as existing code.
```

/speckit-constitution — Amend the existing VisualCore constitution specifically for Round 8, without deleting or weakening any existing requirements from README.md, CLAUDE.md, round2.md or rounds 3..7. Read actual source code and prior round convergence/device records before amending. Add enforceable principles: paid-once complete offline 3D games; no ads, advertising SDKs, tracking identifiers, IAP or subscriptions; no AI-generated images or hand modeled/painted hero assets; all visual effects written as procedural geometry, GLSL ES 3 shader programs, deterministic particles, fluids or analytic paths through the already-existing VisualCore → EGL/OpenGL ES → ANGLE's Metal backend. Preserve vendor forks and signing restrictions. Require independent CPU solver witnesses, 100 real content levels per proposed game, accessible interactions and distinct mechanics verified against the entire portfolio. Require all eight Spec Kit steps (specify/clarify/plan/checklist/tasks/analyze/implement/converge) for 12 incremental shared features and 250 game features; repeat implement + converge until real tests prove completion. Implementation + host/simulator verification must finish before a new implementation-lock manifest permits physical testing. Then test all 25 apps on D1, then D2, then D3, never update D3 from iPadOS 26.5. Device tests and market claims must cite actual evidence. No autonomous authority for Apple signing, login, billing, contract agreement, physical device permission, remote pushes outside owner standing approvals or release. Resolve routine ambiguities autonomously in written ADRs; do not invent success. Preserve this amendment with a dated constitution version and requirement traceability.

## 4. Portfolio boundaries, previous-round gate and simulator/device split
- **MANDATORY PRECONDITION:** `round7.md` full implementation lock, 25 apps × three device outcomes, test provenance and final convergence complete. Verify hashes and logs; a nonexistent earlier round MUST block this one.
- **IMPLEMENTATION FIRST:** execute Round 8 shared features F01-F11; implement each of the 25 complete apps with all ten independent scoped Spec Kit feature flows; run macOS host, Linux-where-possible, iOS 26.5 and 27.2 simulator build and XCUITest. Physical device runs are forbidden until suite lock.
- **Physical device pass:** all 25 on D1 consecutively, then all 25 on D2, then all 25 on D3 without updating D3, through signed automation build, `xcrun devicectl`, JSON results, `xcodebuild` `.xcresult`, screen captures and thermal/frame evidence. Distinguish genuine pass, unsupported, failed, and owner blocked; skipped is never success.
- **Privacy:** no online gameplay, ad identifiers, app trackers, IAP, subscriptions, Apple account prompts, image-generation calls or licensed third-party art dependency. Shipping release must omit automation symbols; user-licensed fonts/system icons are okay if audited, not hero art.
- **Originality:** no near-identical products. Before release, prove each player goal/input/progression/visual metaphor is not merely a palette-swapped duplicate of another game in Round 1, 2 or this round.
- **Owner-only:** never alter signing teams/certificates, update D3, agree to commerce/legal terms or execute irreversible App Store publishing. A blocked item is marked honestly with next exact human step, not permission bypass.

## 5. Complete game-by-game implementation blueprints and per-feature Spec Kit commands
### 01. Origami Observatory — complete proposed implementation design (`R08-G01`)
**Source:** `G307`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.1 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Reconfigure a folding dome so its star apertures align. **Signature animated environment:** articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. **Core abstraction:** room hinge graph.
#### 5.1.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Reconfigure a folding dome so its star apertures align. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `room hinge graph` computational rules, visual `articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` and player control arrangement `Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.1.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** world transforms of connected panels rotate around shared manifold hinges. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Reconfigure a folding dome so its star apertures align. Normalize input into `OrigamiObservatoryAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 5 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** hinge-state graph search plus reachability and collision certificates. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.1.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable room hinge graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with reconfigure a folding dome so its star apertures align; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative room hinge graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.1.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `OrigamiObservatoryScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `OrigamiObservatoryParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `e1faca90d7b0` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.1.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.1.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `articulated triangulated roof sections framed by night sky; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND8_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round8/origami-observatory/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND8_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round8/origami-observatory/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND8_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round8/origami-observatory/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. **Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 02. Halo Locksmith — complete proposed implementation design (`R08-G02`)
**Source:** `G204`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.08 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Adjust concentric light gates until a spectral key can travel through them. **Signature animated environment:** iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. **Core abstraction:** ray/wave optical graph.
#### 5.2.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, sdf optics and gradient materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Adjust concentric light gates until a spectral key can travel through them. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `ray/wave optical graph` computational rules, visual `iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` and player control arrangement `Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.2.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Adjust concentric light gates until a spectral key can travel through them. Normalize input into `HaloLocksmithAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** route or phase-align rays through specified optical stations. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded ray graph traversal with plane intersections and reflection/refraction validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.2.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable ray/wave optical graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with adjust concentric light gates until a spectral key can travel through them; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative ray/wave optical graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.2.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** projected caustics, beam cylinders, chromatic dispersion approximations. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `HaloLocksmithScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `HaloLocksmithParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `f9b1a11b01ea` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.2.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.2.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk

Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `iridescent halos and soft-edged beam volumes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.

Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. **Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 03. Tesseract Lanterns — complete proposed implementation design (`R08-G03`)
**Source:** `G210`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.08 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Reorient rotating cube lanterns to illuminate inaccessible dimensional corners. **Signature animated environment:** layered 4D projection shadows and neon luminous planes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. **Core abstraction:** ray/wave optical graph.
#### 5.3.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees layered 4d projection shadows and neon luminous planes; analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, sdf optics and gradient materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Reorient rotating cube lanterns to illuminate inaccessible dimensional corners. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `ray/wave optical graph` computational rules, visual `layered 4D projection shadows and neon luminous planes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` and player control arrangement `Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.3.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Reorient rotating cube lanterns to illuminate inaccessible dimensional corners. Normalize input into `TesseractLanternsAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** route or phase-align rays through specified optical stations. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded ray graph traversal with plane intersections and reflection/refraction validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.3.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting layered 4D projection shadows and neon luminous planes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable ray/wave optical graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with reorient rotating cube lanterns to illuminate inaccessible dimensional corners; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative ray/wave optical graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.3.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** projected caustics, beam cylinders, chromatic dispersion approximations. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** layered 4D projection shadows and neon luminous planes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `TesseractLanternsScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `TesseractLanternsParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `dca6d442acd6` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.3.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

**Frame/thermal stress risk:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `layered 4D projection shadows and neon luminous planes; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.

**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 04. Infinity Fold — complete proposed implementation design (`R08-G04`)
**Source:** `G430`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.07 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Rotate linked panels to make an impossible-looking continuous walkway. **Signature animated environment:** dramatic perspective-sensitive geometry across voids; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. **Core abstraction:** hinged face net.
#### 5.4.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees dramatic perspective-sensitive geometry across voids; reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Rotate linked panels to make an impossible-looking continuous walkway. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `hinged face net` computational rules, visual `dramatic perspective-sensitive geometry across voids; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials` and player control arrangement `Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.4.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** R_i(θ_i) transforms adjacent faces around shared edge; reject 3D triangle intersections. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Rotate linked panels to make an impossible-looking continuous walkway. Normalize input into `InfinityFoldAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** fold a legal geometric net into a connected target solid without self-collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over discretized hinge states with swept triangle intersection. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** folding singularities, Z-fighting, hidden face gestures. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.4.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting dramatic perspective-sensitive geometry across voids; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable hinged face net handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with rotate linked panels to make an impossible-looking continuous walkway; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative hinged face net predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.4.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted polyhedron mesh, glowing seams and easing hinge transforms. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** dramatic perspective-sensitive geometry across voids; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `InfinityFoldScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `InfinityFoldParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `4ae14a3f7d87` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.4.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 05. Mirrorfold Lab — complete proposed implementation design (`R08-G05`)
**Source:** `G438`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.07 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Fold reflective polygons until a beam loops back to its source. **Signature animated environment:** spinning triangular mirror arrays under saturated beams; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. **Core abstraction:** hinged face net.
#### 5.5.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees spinning triangular mirror arrays under saturated beams; reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Fold reflective polygons until a beam loops back to its source. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `hinged face net` computational rules, visual `spinning triangular mirror arrays under saturated beams; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials` and player control arrangement `Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.5.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** R_i(θ_i) transforms adjacent faces around shared edge; reject 3D triangle intersections. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Fold reflective polygons until a beam loops back to its source. Normalize input into `MirrorfoldLabAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** fold a legal geometric net into a connected target solid without self-collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over discretized hinge states with swept triangle intersection. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** folding singularities, Z-fighting, hidden face gestures. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.5.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting spinning triangular mirror arrays under saturated beams; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable hinged face net handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with fold reflective polygons until a beam loops back to its source; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative hinged face net predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.5.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted polyhedron mesh, glowing seams and easing hinge transforms. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** spinning triangular mirror arrays under saturated beams; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `MirrorfoldLabScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `MirrorfoldLabParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `0c10cfa44009` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.5.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.
